rules.title: FEHA source-of-income discrimination ban
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot refuse to rent to, or apply different terms to, applicants or tenants because of their source of income, including Section 8 vouchers, SSI, rental assistance or wages. They must also complete paperwork and allow inspections required by rental assistance programs and cannot advertise "No Section 8."
rules.quoted_span: California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”).
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.key_value: Source of income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) is a protected characteristic

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied home renting to one additional person

rules.coverage_conditions: Covers most housing accommodations in California.
rules.exemptions: Owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics (but not make discriminatory statements or ads); senior housing may be age-limited.
rules.penalty: Remedies include out-of-pocket losses, injunction, access to the housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.

rules.title: FEHA limits on criminal-history screening
rules.requirement: Landlords may check criminal history but cannot consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot have blanket bans on people with criminal history. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to being a good tenant and not a threat to others' health, safety or property.
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.key_value: No blanket bans; no arrests without conviction, sealed/expunged or juvenile records

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied home renting to one additional person

rules.coverage_conditions: Covers most housing providers and tenant screening companies in California.
rules.conflict_note: The page does not give a statute section; Gov. Code § 12952 is inferred as the criminal-history provision of FEHA.

parsed.doc_summary: California Civil Rights Department housing page on FEHA. It supports two state screening-restriction rules: the source-of-income (incl. Section 8) protection and the limits on criminal-history screening. Other content covers general discrimination, accommodations and complaint process. It says CRD has no jurisdiction over evictions, rent control or deposit returns.
